translationRepairs: Na's great-grandson Ke Hui became Wei's western guardian general, colonel who pacified the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang hosts.
Na's great-great-grandson Ke Hui became Wei's western guardian general, colonel who pacified the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang hosts.
那玄孫柯回 uses 玄孫, the fourth-generation descendant (great-great-grandson), not 曾孫 (great-grandson). The proposed kinship term is accurate.
Na's great-grandson Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Chief Commander of the Western Qiang.
Na's great-great-grandson Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Chief Commander of the Western Qiang.
The literal field repeats the same kinship error: 玄孫 is great-great-grandson. The replacement matches the Chinese.
Ma Heluo in Yizhong's ranks was a scholar; when Zhang Cao propped up Shi Shi he defected to become Cao's secretariat draftsman.
Ma Heluo in Yizhong's ranks was a scholar; when Zhang Chai propped up Shi Shi he defected to become Chai's secretariat draftsman.
The person is 張豺; 豺 is Chái, not Cáo. Replacing Cao/Chai in this sentence restores the name without changing the rest of the rendering.
Among Yizhong's followers Ma Heluo was learned and literary; when Zhang Cao aided Shi Shi he abandoned Yizhong for Cao, who appointed him Gentleman of the Secretariat.
Among Yizhong's followers Ma Heluo was learned and literary; when Zhang Chai aided Shi Shi he abandoned Yizhong for Chai, who appointed him Gentleman of the Secretariat.
Literal 張豺 / 歸豺 likewise requires Zhang Chai and Chai, not Zhang Cao and Cao.
After Cao collapsed he crawled back, and voices clamored for his execution.
After Chai collapsed he crawled back, and voices clamored for his execution.
豺敗 names Zhang Chai’s fall. 'Cao' is a wrong reading of 豺; 'Chai' is the correct short form.
When Cao fell he returned; all urged killing him.
When Chai fell he returned; all urged killing him.
The literal 'When Cao fell' mistranslates 豺敗; Chai is the right name.
Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as general who spreads might, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.
Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as general of agile cavalry, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.
石祗 appointed Xiang 驃騎將軍, General of Agile Cavalry, not a 'general who spreads might' (that would be 揚武). The office name is the real error.
When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General Who Spreads Might, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang Commissioner Bearing Credentials, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.

驃騎將軍 is General of Agile Cavalry, so the proposed cavalry title is right, but 使持節 is a credential, not an inspectorate; 豫州刺史 is the inspector post. The after still called 使持節 a 'credential-bearing inspector'.

His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng and Heina of Lüeyang flanking the van and wings, Lian Qi of Nan'an on the right, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan with Quan Yi as advisers.

His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng of Lüeyang over the left division, Lian Qi of Nan'an over the right, Heina of Lüeyang in the van, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan of Taiyuan with Quan Yi of Lüeyang as advisers.
The Chinese assigns 伏子成左部帥, 斂岐右部帥, 黑那前部帥, 強白後部帥, and gives 太原薛贊 and 略陽權翼 as 參軍. The original garbles those posts and drops the two origins; the replacement restores them.

When wanderers under Gu Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.

When wanderers under Guo Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.
流人郭斁: the surname 郭 is Guo, not Gu.

More than a thousand displaced persons led by Gu Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.

More than a thousand displaced persons led by Guo Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.
The same 郭斁 requires Guo Yi in the literal field.
Yao Chang, courtesy Maomao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
Yao Chang, courtesy Jingmao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
萇字景茂: 景 is Jing, so the courtesy name is Jingmao, not Maomao.
Chang's courtesy name was Maomao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
Chang's courtesy name was Jingmao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
The literal courtesy name must likewise be Jingmao for 景茂.

He climbed through left guard general, a chain of western prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.

He climbed through left guard general, a chain of prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.
The prefecture list is 隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風. 武威 is Wuwei and 巴西 is Baxi; 'Weiba' and 'Brazil' are corrupt, and the commanderies are not all western.

He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.

He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
Literal Weiba/Brazil are the same corruptions of 武威 and 巴西; Wuwei and Baxi are the correct names.

Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, against Fucheng, and had his brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally Beidi tribes—more than fifty thousand households came over.

Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his elder paternal cousin Yao Lan, General Who Supports the State, against Fucheng, and had his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally the Rong and Chinese of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households came over.
輔國 is the abbreviated generalship, 從兄 an elder paternal cousin, and 兄 an elder brother, so those proposed fixes are real. The after still renders 北地戎夏 as 'Beidi tribes', dropping 夏.

Xiang soon moved to Beiqu, intending to take Guanzhong; he advanced and camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, to seize territory around Fucheng, and ordered his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu to gather Rong and Xia of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households submitted.

Xiang soon moved to Beiqu, intending to take Guanzhong; he advanced and camped at Xingcheng, sent his elder paternal cousin, the General Who Supports the State Yao Lan, to seize territory around Fucheng, and ordered his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu to gather Rong and Xia of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households submitted.
The literal replacement correctly expands 輔國 to General Who Supports the State and 從兄 to elder paternal cousin, while already keeping 戎夏 as Rong and Xia.
When the Qiang host closed in, Xiang flew into a rage, charged forward, and met them at Sanyuan.
When Deng Qiang's troops closed in, Xiang flew into a rage, charged forward, and met them at Sanyuan.
After 苻堅、鄧羌等要之, 會羌師來逼 uses 羌 for Deng Qiang’s force, not the Qiang people (Xiang’s own ethnicity). Reading 羌師 as Deng Qiang’s troops is the sense the sequence requires.
When Chang usurped the title, he posthumously enfeoffed Xiang as Wei Wuwang and made Xiang's grandson Yanding Marquis of Dongcheng.
When Chang usurped the title, he posthumously named Xiang King Wu of Wei and made Xiang's grandson Yanding Marquis of Dongcheng.
追諡魏武王 confers a posthumous title, King Wu of Wei, not an enfeoffment (封 is used only for 延定).

Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju through Zhang Qian, and column leaders from Wang Qinlu to Dang Shan.

Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian, and column leaders Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, and Dang Shan.
The Chinese names six 參軍 (王據 through 張乾) and nine 帥 (王欽盧 through 黨刪). Collapsing them to 'through/to' omits those appointees; restoring the names is required.
Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's tile.
Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's title.
拜散騎常侍 is an office title; 'tile' is a typo for 'title'.

In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and rechristened the metropolis with a court spelling that punned on Chang'an while invoking lasting peace.
In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and renamed the capital Chang'an to Chang'an, 'Enduring Peace'.

The source does rename the capital (改長安曰常安), so the original paraphrase is incomplete, but the proposed after cannot stand: it inserts Chinese graphs into the English field. The revised line states the new name in romanization with the meaning 'Enduring Peace'.
At the Shanggui feast Gu Chengshan of Nan'an urged, "Our land is rich, rugged, and crowded with talent—made for war.
At the Shanggui feast Gucheng Shen of Nan'an urged, "Our land is rich, rugged, and crowded with talent—made for war.
南安人古成詵: 古成 is the compound surname and 詵 the given name Shen. 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides the name.

Thereupon he feasted officers at Shanggui; Gu Chengshan of Nan'an advanced and said: "My province's people are prosperous and the terrain perilous; heroes stand thick as a forest—it is a land suited to arms.

Thereupon he feasted officers at Shanggui; Gucheng Shen of Nan'an advanced and said: "My province's people are prosperous and the terrain perilous; heroes stand thick as a forest—it is a land suited to arms.
The literal field has the same misdivision of 古成詵; Gucheng Shen is the correct English name.
Yin Wei and Yao Huang pressed Gu Chengshan: "Years later Deng still breathes; predators flock on every side; Chinese and tribesmen hedge—what next?"
Yin Wei and Yao Huang pressed Gucheng Shen: "Years later Deng still breathes; predators flock on every side; Chinese and tribesmen hedge—what next?"
尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵: the addressee is Gucheng Shen, not Gu Chengshan.
Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gu Chengshan: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe yet years have not destroyed him; villains perch like owls everywhere rallying; Yi and Xia alike waver—what is to be done?"
Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gucheng Shen: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe yet years have not destroyed him; villains perch like owls everywhere rallying; Yi and Xia alike waver—what is to be done?"
The literal vocative is likewise 古成詵 and must be Gucheng Shen.
Chengshan retorted, "Clear rewards and sure punishments win every able man—why fear the Di outlaw!"
Shen retorted, "Clear rewards and sure punishments win every able man—why fear the Di outlaw!"
詵曰 uses the given name Shen. 'Chengshan' is a leftover from the misread compound surname.

Chengshan said: "Our lord's stratagem knows no bound; trust rewards and certain punishments move all worthy men to joyful allegiance—why worry the great enterprise will not succeed or the Di bandit will not perish!"

Shen said: "Our lord's stratagem knows no bound; trust rewards and certain punishments move all worthy men to joyful allegiance—why worry the great enterprise will not succeed or the Di bandit will not perish!"
Literal 詵曰 should be 'Shen said', not 'Chengshan said'.
Chengshan answered, "The triple Qin heartland is heaven's granary—our lord holds eight shares in ten.
Shen answered, "The triple Qin heartland is heaven's granary—our lord holds eight shares in ten.
The next 詵曰 is the same speaker Shen.
Chengshan said: "The three Qins are Heaven's storehouse; our lord already holds eight tenths.
Shen said: "The three Qins are Heaven's storehouse; our lord already holds eight tenths.
Literal 詵曰 again names Shen, not Chengshan.
Lan Niu of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.
Lan Du of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.
蘭犢: 犢 is dú. Lan Niu would be 牛; the name is Lan Du.
Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Niu split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Niu sent envoys begging rescue.
Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Du split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys begging rescue.
犢遣使請救 continues the same name 蘭犢 / Du, not Niu.
Lan Niu fell too, men and mounts included.
Lan Du fell too, men and mounts included.
又擒蘭犢 is capture of Lan Du, not Lan Niu.
He also seized Lan Niu and gathered his soldiers and horses.
He also seized Lan Du and gathered his soldiers and horses.
The literal seizure line is the same 蘭犢, correctly Lan Du.

Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Poluo, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.

Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Pochu, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.
冠威彌姐婆觸: 觸 is chù, so Pochu, not Poluo.

After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Poluo, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.

After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Pochu, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.
The literal name of 彌姐婆觸 must likewise be Mizijie Pochu.
Chang was about to march to save them; Minister over the Masses Yao Min, left servant Yin Wei and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near Watting; Your Majesty ought not lightly move."

Chang was about to march to save them; Director of the Secretariat Yao Min, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat Yin Wei and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near Watting; Your Majesty ought not lightly move."
尚書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not 司徒 (Minister over the Masses); 左僕射 is Left Supervisor of the Secretariat, not 'left servant'.
Thereupon he left Minister over the Masses Yao Min holding Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage at Dajie, taking it.
Thereupon he left Director of the Secretariat Yao Min holding Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage at Dajie, taking it.
尚書令姚旻 is again Director of the Secretariat, not Minister over the Masses.

He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; two-plus ten thousand households of Tujue Luochuan in Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.

He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; more than twenty thousand households of the Tuge of Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.
天水屠各 is the Tuge, not 'Tujue Luochuan', and 二萬餘戶 is more than twenty thousand households.
At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tujue herders in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.
At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tuge tribesmen in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.
Idiomatic 'Tujue' anachronistically names the Türks; 屠各 are the Tuge.
Dou Yuan of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households and won western pacifier general.
Dou Yang of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households and won western pacifier general.
南羌竇鴦: 鴦 is yāng, so Dou Yang, not Dou Yuan.
Southern Qiang Dou Yuan led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
Southern Qiang Dou Yang led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
The literal name of 竇鴦 is likewise Dou Yang.
Eastern guardian Gou Yao gripped Rebel-Wan keeps and connived with Fu Deng.
Eastern guardian Gou Yao gripped Niwan Fort and connived with Fu Deng.
逆萬堡 is the fort name Niwan; translating 逆 as 'Rebel' invents a gloss the toponym does not carry here.
General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Rebel-Wan fort and secretly drew Fu Deng.
General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Niwan Fort and secretly drew Fu Deng.
Literal Rebel-Wan fort is the same false gloss of 逆萬堡; Niwan Fort is the place name.
After crushing Deng east of Anding he hosted a triumph; generals muttered, "Had General Wei Wuwang—your brother Yao Xiang—still commanded, Deng would be ash; you shut yourself in too tight."
After crushing Deng east of Anding he hosted a triumph; generals muttered, "Had King Wu of Wei—your late brother Yao Xiang—still commanded, Deng would be ash; you shut yourself in too tight."
若值魏武王 cites Yao Xiang’s posthumous royal title King Wu of Wei, not a general named Wei Wuwang.
Fu Deng's General Who Spreads Might Moyifu led six thousand households to surrender and was appointed credential-bearing inspector, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Duke of Gaoping.
Fu Deng's General of Agile Cavalry Moyifu led six thousand households to surrender and was appointed Commissioned with Credentials, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Duke of Gaoping.
苻登驃騎將軍 is General of Agile Cavalry, and 使持節 is a credential, not an inspectorate. Both proposed corrections match the Chinese.
When Xing neared Kongkong Fort, Dou Chong's ring broke without a blow.
When Xing neared Hukong Fort, Dou Chong's ring broke without a blow.
比至胡空堡: the place is Hukong Fort; Kongkong drops 胡.
By the time he reached Kongkong Fort of the Hu, Chong's siege dissolved of itself.
By the time he reached Hukong Fort, Chong's siege dissolved of itself.
胡空堡 is one toponym, not 'Kongkong Fort of the Hu'.
Deng heard Xing was bound for Kongkong Fort and withdrew; Xing thereupon raided Pingliang, took great booty, and returned—all as Chang had planned.
